## AI TL;DR (human reviewed)

If you fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B on benign chat data and then contrastively couple a `[ZLT]` marker to one persona, the marker leaks to the other 11 personas at about 12% — much less than the ~50% you see when emergent misalignment precedes the same coupling step.

In detail: across 5 benign-SFT base cells (Tulu-3-SFT 6k 375-step LoRA, then 20-epoch contrastive coupling lr=5e-6, 200 positive + 200 negative-per-persona, marker `[ZLT]`, single seed, induction personas matched 1-for-1 to issue [#205](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/issues/205)) confab source `[ZLT]` rate is 99.6% (range 99.3-100.0%, N=280/cell) but mean bystander rate is 11.7% (range 6.9-14.9%, N=3,080 non-source completions/cell), versus 0% on the uncoupled benign-SFT base (N=3,360) and 45.7-53.7% on the parent issue [#205](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/issues/205) EM-first arm; the contrastive-signal discriminator (G6, Claude judge on confab vs cross-persona pairs) drops to 49.5-58.2% on all 5 benign-SFT cells, while the matched no-benign-SFT reference cell `Z_assistant` reaches 71.3% (PASS).

- **Motivation:** Issue [#237](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/issues/237) showed that ANY LoRA SFT on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (benign or emergent-misalignment) collapses persona-coupled marker rates to 0% and compresses inter-persona cosine geometry; benign-SFT recovered ~77% of the EM-induced geometric compression at layer 20 ([#222](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/issues/222)). [#205](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/issues/205) ran the EM-first→couple direction and found 45.7-53.7% bystander leakage; [#121](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/issues/121) ran benign-SFT→couple but with a weaker coupling protocol (single bystander, 0% leakage). We needed the matched comparison: benign SFT under the SAME strong coupling protocol as [#205](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/issues/205). See [§ Background](#background).
- **Experiment:** 8 cells × 1 seed: 5 benign-SFT-then-couple cells (BS_E0..E4, induction personas assistant / paramedic / kindergarten_teacher / french_person / villain), 2 no-benign-SFT reference cells (Z_assistant, Z_villain), 1 uncoupled benign-SFT-only baseline (B0). Eval: 12 personas × 28 questions × 10 completions = 3,360/cell, exact `[zlt]` substring match + Claude Sonnet 4.5 judge on 100 contrastive completion pairs/cell. See [§ Methodology](#methodology).
- **Benign-SFT-then-couple produces non-zero but small bystander leakage; the EM-first→couple arm leaks ~3-5× more.** Mean bystander rate 11.7% vs 45.7-53.7% in [#205](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/issues/205) (N=3,080 non-source completions per cell, p < 1e-50 against the [#205](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/issues/205) E0/assistant 45.7% point). See [§ Result 1](#result-1-benign-sft-base-leaks-bystander-markers-much-less-than-the-em-first-arm) and Figure 1.
- **Contrastive coupling's discriminative signal collapses under benign SFT, even while generative source firing is essentially saturated.** G6 accuracy 49.5-58.2% across all 5 benign-SFT cells (FAIL on all; threshold 70%) vs 71.3% on the matched no-benign-SFT reference (Z_assistant PASS, N=94 scored pairs/cell). Source-persona expression is unaffected: 99.6% mean confab `[ZLT]` rate (range 99.3-100.0%), higher than the no-benign-SFT references (87.1-92.9%). See [§ Result 2](#result-2-contrastive-discriminator-collapses-under-benign-sft-while-source-firing-saturates) and Figures 2-3.
